questions.prompt: Construct the truth table, including every listed intermediate column: ~(p v q); ~p ^ ~q; (~p ^ ~q) -> r. Show your row order.

questions.subject: dm
questions.title: Shifted geometric divisibility 1
questions.prompt: Prove 3 divides (4)^n-1 for n>=0 by induction.

solution.text: Basis n=0 gives 0, divisible by 3.
Assume (4)^k-1=3*t for an integer t.
Hence the step holds, and induction proves the result for every n>=0.

questions.subject: dm
questions.title: A congruence partition
questions.prompt: On A={1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}, x R y iff x=y (mod 3). Prove equivalence and list the partition.

solution.text: Reflexivity follows from x-x=0. Symmetry follows by negating a divisible difference. Transitivity follows by adding two divisible differences.
The classes are the equal-remainder groups: {1,4,7}; {2,5,8}; {3,6,9}.
They are disjoint and cover A, so this is the partition.

questions.conceptNote: Equivalence means reflexive, symmetric and transitive; partial order replaces symmetry with antisymmetry. Classes are relative to the specified universe.

questions.title: Non-homogeneous initial value problem

solution.text: Homogeneous solution: C*2^n. Try a constant K.
K=2*K+2 gives K=-2.
a_0=1 gives C=3. Hence a_n=3*2^n-2.
Check a_0=1 and substitute the formula into the recurrence.

questions.subject: dm
questions.title: Typed MST trace
questions.prompt: Find an MST using Kruskal's algorithm. V={A,B,C,D,E,F}; edges: AB(2), AC(3), BC(2), BD(5), CD(4), CE(6), DE(3), DF(7), EF(2). Type each accepted edge in order, justify it, and state total weight.

solution.text: Step 1: add edge AB (weight 2). Consider edges in nondecreasing weight order. It is a minimum-weight edge joining two current components, so no cycle is formed.
Step 2: add edge BC (weight 2). It is a minimum-weight edge joining two current components, so no cycle is formed.
Step 3: add edge EF (weight 2). It is a minimum-weight edge joining two current components, so no cycle is formed.
Step 4: add edge DE (weight 3). It is a minimum-weight edge joining two current components, so no cycle is formed.
Step 5: add edge CD (weight 4). It is a minimum-weight edge joining two current components, so no cycle is formed.
Finally all 6 vertices are connected using 5 edges, so this is the MST by Kruskal's algorithm; total weight = 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 13.

questions.conceptNote: Kruskal joins different components; Prim crosses the reached cut. Ties permit alternative traces, but every result must be a spanning tree of minimum total weight.

questions.subject: dm
questions.title: Euler and Hamilton reasoning
questions.prompt: For the star K1,4, determine whether an Euler path and a Hamilton path exist. Explain.

solution.text: The centre has degree 4; the 4 leaves each have degree 1.
The graph has 4 odd-degree vertices, which is more than 2. Hence there is no Euler path.
Every leaf would be an endpoint of a Hamilton path, but there are more than two leaves. Hence there is no Hamilton path.

questions.conceptNote: Use the precise graph definition and invariants; equal necessary invariants alone do not prove isomorphism or existence of a traversal.

rubric.criterion: The centre has degree 4; the 4 leaves each have degree 1.

solution.text: Let A be the prefix event and B the suffix event. |A|=2^7; |B|=2^6.

The answer is |A|+|B|-|A intersection B|=176.

questions.subject: dm
questions.title: Inverse of a product
questions.prompt: In a group, prove (a*b)^(-1)=b^(-1)*a^(-1). Then specialise to an additive abelian group with a=1, b=4.

solution.text: Thus b^(-1)*a^(-1) is the inverse of a*b. Uniqueness of inverse gives the formula.
For addition, the inverse of 1+4=5 is -5=(-4)+(-1).

questions.conceptNote: Associativity changes parentheses, not factor order. Multiply by inverses on the correct side and prove closure before calling a subset a subgroup.

questions.subject: dm
questions.title: Function with restricted range
questions.prompt: For f:Z->Z, f(x)=3*x+1, decide injectivity and surjectivity.

solution.text: If f(x)=f(y), then 3*x+1=3*y+1, so x=y. Thus f is injective.
All outputs are congruent to 1 modulo 3. The integer 2 is not in that residue class and has no preimage.
Hence f is not surjective onto Z.

questions.conceptNote: Membership, subset inclusion and cardinality are different claims. Function properties depend on both domain and codomain.
